mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants anticipate continued monetary stimulus.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 10.0%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 10.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST > 550.0) and retail sales (RSAFS > 330000.0) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST>550 and RSAFS>330000), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a near-zero interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%), the market anticipates continued monetary stimulus, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations adjust to low discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS > 130000.0) reflects a healthy labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 130000.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 600.0 units indicate strong residential construction activity, signaling a resilient economy and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 600.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent expansion in industrial production (INDPRO > 90.0) and GDP growth (GDPC1 > 13500.0) indicates robust supply chain activity and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved corporate earnings outlooks.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (INDPRO>90 and GDPC1>13500), or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220.0) signals an environment where the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
